newsitem.title: GERMANY: Kohl drops engagement in Paris to stay at home.
newsitem.headline: Kohl drops engagement in Paris to stay at home.

text.p: German Chancellor Helmut Kohl has dropped plans to travel to Paris on Wednesday to address the parliamentary assembly of the Western European Union, a government spokesman said.

The spokesman said on Tuesday Kohl was staying in Bonn because Finance Minister Theo Waigel, locked in a battle with the Bundesbank over plans to revalue Germany's gold reserves to improve public finances before joining a single European currency, was to make an important statement in parliament.
"It was decided yesterday that Kohl should stay here in Bonn to be there for the government declaration to be read in parliament tomorrow," the spokesman said.
Kohl will fly to Washington later on Wednesday to attend 50th anniversary celebrations of the Marshall Plan that helped rebuild Europe's economies after World War Two.
The cancellation was not linked to the election of a new Socialist-led government in France, a German embassy spokesman in Paris said.
Kohl will meet Socialist Prime Minister Lionel Jospin along with conservative President Jacques Chirac at the next regular Franco-German summit rescheduled for June 13 in Poitiers, in western France.
